title: The Crows and the Hawk

full_text:
In an ancient grove of walnut trees lived a large flock of crows who had established a peaceful commonwealth. One summer, a fierce hunting hawk took up his perch upon an overhanging granite crag above the grove, sweeping down daily to attack any lone crow that ventured into the open fields.

The elders of the flock called a general assembly. A young, impetuous crow shouted: 'Let our fiercest warrior fly up to the crag and challenge the hawk to single combat!'

An aged, venerable crow shook his head: 'A single crow cannot withstand the hawk's razor talons and hooked beak. But where individual strength fails, united numbers conquer. When the hawk attacks again, let no bird fly alone; let forty of us take wing simultaneously, form a rotating circle around him, and blind his vision with the dust of our wings!'

The next morning, the hawk plunged toward the grove. Instantly, forty crows took flight in coordinated formation!

They surrounded the predator, cawing with deafening unison, darting in and out from every angle, pecking at his wings, and beating the air until the confused hawk could neither focus his attack nor maneuver his broad wings.

Battered, disoriented, and exhausted by the united defense, the hawk broke through the formation and fled across the mountains, never daring to return to the walnut grove.

The crows returned to their boughs in triumph, having learned that collective unity is an impenetrable fortress against tyranny.
moral: United cooperation and collective vigilance protect the community against the fiercest predators.
